title: Harvest AI cost optimization recommendation deltas
objective: Produce a concise before/after cost model for Harvest AI and recommend a prioritized set of Redwood Optimize changes that deliver high-confidence run-rate savings while keeping chat-generation quality loss <1% on the customer eval set.
executive_summary: Harvest AI currently spends an estimated $142k/month on inference for their mix of chat + embeddings workloads. We propose a stepped program (prefix caching + smarter routing + int8 quantization for non-critical endpoints + targeted batching) that reduces expected monthly spend to $73.2k (approx $825k annualized). Primary risks: ~0.4–0.9% quality delta on certain NLU intents; rollout mitigations and canary evaluation recommended.
baseline_breakdown: Chat generation (gpt-3.8-xxl variant): $102k/mo; Embeddings (onnx-sparse): $22k/mo; Low-latency inference for search rerank: $18k/mo. Peak concurrency sizing: 160 concurrent sessions; average seq length (chat): 650 tokens; 95p lat: 180ms.
recommended_changes: 1) Deploy prefix/KV caching for 40% of returning sessions (saves ~22% of chat token cost). 2) Route experimental low-priority batch workloads to cheaper region instances (saves ~12% of total). 3) Quantize non-mainline models to INT8 and enable mixed-precision for generator (saves ~18% of chat cost). 4) Increase dynamic batching windows for embeddings (saves ~9% on embeddings). 5) Introduce a distilled 6B fallback for low-criticality assistant responses (saves ~8% when hit).
quality_regression_estimate: Aggregate expected quality regression: 0.6% on Harvest eval set (measured by intent-F1 drop). Breakdown: INT8 quantization: ~0.35% delta; distillation fallback: 0.2%; routing/batching: negligible but monitor latency tail effects.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): small-canary for KV caching on 5% of traffic + end-to-end evaluation. Phase 1 (4 weeks): enable INT8 for non-critical endpoints and embeddings quantization in staging; compare eval metrics. Phase 2 (6 weeks): expand caching to 40% and configure region routing policies; enable distilled fallback behind A/B flags. Phase 3: full rollout with continuous monitoring and automatic rollback triggers tied to intent-F1 and 95th latency.
sensitivity_analysis: Three scenarios run against current traffic mix: A) High adoption (80% effective): annual savings ~$1.05M. B) Moderate adoption (50%): annual savings ~$625k. C) Low adoption / quality rollback (20%): annual savings ~$250k but delayed by 3 months for rework. Also ran spot-price risk: +20% GPU price reduces savings by ~16%.
open_questions: 1) Can Harvest provide a 50k-sample prompt set to better estimate INT8 regressions? 2) Are there regulatory constraints for routing embeddings cross-region? 3) SLA expectations for 95p latency after batching increases?

notes_to_self: Draft contains a few rough numbers (we estimated hit rates conservatively). Need to re-run model-specific kernel benchmark for the distilled 6B to tighten the 8% savings estimate. Customer is price-sensitive; emphasize short-term wins (caching + routing) first.

Customer asked whether Redwood can run a 2-week pilot with no commit — recommend using dedicated trial credits + telemetry export.
